function: CSI compression at the UE and recovery at the BS (CSI feedback) for dual-polarized massive MIMO channels, exploiting the correlation between polarizations (p. 5-7).
system: FDD downlink, BS with 32 dual-polarized antennas, single-antenna UE, 3.5 GHz, 10 MHz, 32 subbands; no RIS (p. 6, Table I on p. 21).
method: Disentangled-representation autoencoder with convolutional attention and separate FC layers; CLUB mutual-information regularizer; trained offline with MSE loss (p. 16-17).
data_channel: Simulated 3GPP TR 38.901 CDL-A/B/C (CDL-D for LoS) at 3.5 GHz, 100,000 training samples; QuaDRiGa data for the generalization test (p. 20, 30).
test_conditions: Default: train and test on the same CDL profile (CDL-A); generalization: train CDL-A, test QuaDRiGa and the reverse; mixed CDL-A/B/C training (p. 30).
baselines: Learned: CsiNet, CRNet, ACRNet-1x/5x (NMSE, p. 22); non-learned: 5G NR Type I and Type II codebooks, compared on achievable rate (p. 31).
metrics: NMSE and its CDF, number of parameters, encoder/decoder inference time, feedback bits, average achievable rate per user with ZF precoding (p. 22-31).
complexity: Parameters 695K (ratio 8) to 160K (ratio 64), 1.481M summed over ratios (Table II, p. 23); encoder/decoder inference time in ms (Fig. 8, p. 24).
q1_support: p. 20: "we generate the training set, validation set, and testing set through CDL channel models defined in 3GPP specification TR 38.901"
q2_support: p. 30: "testing the QuaDRiGa channel on a network trained by the CDL-A channel"
q3_support: p. 31: "three DL-based methods, including CsiNet [19], CRNet [22] and our proposed DiReNet, along with two codebook-based methods, i.e., Type I and Type II [7]"
q4_support: p. 23: "network complexity is measured by the number of parameters"
q5_support: p. 1: "The source code of this paper is available on GitHub: https://github.com/SEUshf/DiReNet"
notes: Version read is the arXiv preprint (arXiv:2403.19185v1); pages refer to that file, which does not print the DOI (the DOI match rests on the file name). Area 2 because the function is CSI compression and feedback. q3: the learned baselines are compared on NMSE (Fig. 7, p. 22), and the non-learned Type I and Type II codebooks only on achievable rate (Fig. 13, p. 31), which is a performance metric of the paper.
